title: A validation error pushes every field below it down the page
foundBy: repository owner (host): "when the border gets color red, the form fields shift down because of the error messages below them. thats distracting?"

evidence.verified: Measured in the built preview at 1280 by 900, submitting the Form pattern with every field empty. Before: Email moved 22px, Plan 22px, Notes 48px, and the form grew from 433px to 481px. After: every field moved 0px and the form height was 477px before and after the submit. A browser test carries the guarantee, because jsdom computes no layout: reverting the change fails `src/components/FormGroup.layout.test.tsx` with `expected 106 to be 84`, the same 22px. `npm run ci` exits 0 with every gate run and 627 tests.

details:
FormGroup renders its error message in flow, below the control. The message appears only once a field is invalid, so every field below it moves down at the moment the user submits.

Measured in the built preview at 1280 by 900, submitting the Form pattern with every field empty: the Email control moves down 22px, the Plan control 22px, and the Notes control 48px. The form grows from 433px to 481px.

The Email field is the exception, and it points at the fix. Its helper text is replaced by the error rather than joined by it, so that row does not change height. A field whose message slot is always occupied does not move.

The choice is a design decision rather than a defect to fix one way. Reserving a message line under every field removes the shift and makes every form permanently taller. Reserving it only after the first submit attempt removes the shift where a user would notice it, at the cost of a rule that depends on form state. Taking the message out of flow avoids both costs and risks it overlapping the field below.

This affects every consumer of FormGroup, not only the pattern it was noticed in.

notes.text: Only visible since CUI-020 made the Form pattern reach its error states. Reserving space would change what the visual gate photographs for every form, so the baseline moves with whichever option wins.

The owner chose reserving the slot, with helper text swapped for the error where a field has one. FormGroup already swapped, so only the reserve was missing. It uses `min-height: 1lh` at the message font size, which is exactly the line the message will occupy rather than a guess at its computed line-height: a first attempt calculated the height from the tokens and left 3px of movement. The cost is one line of height per group, and a form at rest is 44px taller.

The baseline was re-recorded for six captures, all of them measured. `checkbox-group` grows from 200x172 to 200x194 in both themes, because CheckboxGroup renders a FormGroup of its own. `pattern-form` changes 0.9629% and 0.9680%. `pattern-dashboard` changes 6 pixels and 4 pixels, where that same group sits in a column that scrolls, and it never failed the 0.1% threshold. A fresh compare against the fresh baseline reports 0 differing pixels across all 94, so the renders are byte-stable and those counts are the change rather than jitter.
